title: Choose Xerom’s visual world
question: Each direction keeps Xerom black, red and white, starts with the social group experience, and includes a mobile-first booking path. Choose one, steer a re-roll, or take the familiar category standard.

options.label: Race Control Broadcast
options.lineage: live motorsport timing, race-control screens and broadcast graphics
options.thesis: The whole venue feels like a live race night where the crew is the headline and hardware is the proof.
options.viewport: A candid crew moment fills the first screen under crossed red-white lights while a live timing tower frames the scene and a red booking action anchors the edge; mobile becomes one vertical live-race feed.
options.risk: Timing graphics could feel competitive rather than welcoming if the people do not remain visibly dominant.

raised.raise: Every promise must sit beside a real social, hardware or price proof—not decorative telemetry.
Navigation, pricing, booking controls and system states must share one broadcast grammar.
Booking progress and slot state must be immediately legible at every step.
The venue’s crossed-light geometry must recompose into a purposeful mobile frame.

options.label: Pit-Lane Crew Pass
options.lineage: garage passes, paddock contact sheets and independent motorsport zines
options.thesis: Visitors join a local crew for the night, with every section reading like access to another garage bay.
options.viewport: One large laughing group photo owns the first screen, surrounded by tactile contact-sheet fragments, a numbered pit pass and a direct booking strip; mobile reads like a tall event pass.
options.risk: This is the most familiar grounded direction and could become a generic streetwear collage if the real venue and booking flow are not disciplined.

options.label: Starting Grid Sequencer
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm-machine step rows translated into a race-night journey
options.thesis: A night at Xerom becomes a playable sequence—bring the crew, choose the rig, see the value, book the slot.
options.viewport: Social photography and hardware crops sit above one unbroken row of large illuminated steps; on mobile the row scales into a thumb-friendly four-step booking story.
options.case: It beats the others on product clarity and interaction memory, but needs strong photography to identify immediately as Xerom rather than a music tool.
options.risk: The control-panel metaphor could overpower the human warmth if every section becomes a machine interface.

options.label: Night Race Sticker Wall
options.lineage: lowbrow hot-rod panels and lacquered racing sticker walls
options.thesis: Xerom is an overflowing night-race poster where the same crew, rigs and venue compete for attention with joyful force.
options.viewport: A bold illustrated-photo crew tableau dominates, with prices pinned as oversized stickers and the booking action ruled across the base; mobile becomes one dense collectible poster.
options.case: It strongly identifies with Xerom’s energetic Instagram audience, but loses to Race Control on scanning and booking clarity.
options.risk: Crowding can damage accessibility and make changing promotions harder unless text remains live and modular.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.lineage: live scenes rendered as monospace glyph density
options.thesis: The venue appears as a live red-on-black character field.
options.viewport: A moving crew scene becomes a character-grid hero with captions inside the same field.
options.case: It loses both audience identification and immediate service clarity.
options.kept: Total visual-system consistency across every control and state.
options.risk: It obscures faces, venue details and accessibility-critical content.

options.label: Monochrome Proof Pairing
options.thesis: Every claim is paired with a clean visual proof.
options.viewport: A quiet claim-and-proof hero with one restrained accent.
options.case: It directly conflicts with Xerom’s energetic, non-minimal Instagram identity.
options.kept: The discipline that every claim must be visibly proven.
options.risk: It would feel overly corporate and minimal.

options.label: Session Maturity Calendar
options.lineage: a pickling-brine calendar of staged change
options.thesis: Booking states mature through a visible sequence.
options.viewport: Service choices are arranged by stage and availability.
options.case: Its culinary metaphor does not identify with sim racing or explain Xerom faster.
options.kept: Make time, stage and status unmistakable in booking.
options.risk: The metaphor is unrelated to the venue.

options.label: Sleeping Night Circuit
options.lineage: a city folding into a shared night world
options.thesis: Klang’s night folds inward around the illuminated venue.
options.viewport: The venue’s crossed lights reshape a nighttime city field around the crew.
options.case: It loses immediate product clarity and risks making the venue feel fictional.
options.kept: Let the real crossed-light geometry adapt purposefully across viewports.

canonCard.label: Polished Esports Venue
canonCard.thesis: The familiar premium gaming-venue layout, executed cleanly with Xerom photography and colors.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional photo hero with headline, two buttons and service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, but less memorable and more similar to other gaming venues.
